source-integrity.freshness: Q2 2026 primary operating evidence plus Sep-2026 current market valuation
source-integrity.duplicateOriginCollapse: issuer/SEC claims treated by origin; repeated packet projections not counted as independent corroboration
source-integrity.sourceIndependence: SEC/issuer primary facts separated from independent market-data observations

company-underwriting.operatingFinancialTrajectory: Q2 revenue was $17.2B, +1% YoY; Software +5%, Red Hat +11%, Data +19%, while Infrastructure fell 7% and IBM Z fell 42%. H1 operating cash flow rose to $7.8B while H1 free cash flow was roughly flat at $4.8B.
company-underwriting.contractsBacklogCustomersSuppliers: Distributed Infrastructure Power/Storage had nearly $500M backlog; enterprise AI/hybrid-cloud demand is broad but current evidence does not quantify customer concentration or AI-attributable bookings.
company-underwriting.balanceSheetRunwayDebtDilution: Quarter-end cash/restricted cash/marketable securities $8.2B; $10.5B invested in acquisitions YTD; total debt $62.0B. Funding capacity is substantial but acquisition deployment and debt constrain upside confidence.
company-underwriting.governanceCapitalAllocation: Long dividend history and explicit productivity/capital-allocation program coexist with substantial acquisition and >$10B five-year quantum investment commitments whose realized returns remain unproven.
company-underwriting.pricingPowerConcentration: 57.7% GAAP gross margin and diversified software/consulting/infrastructure mix support moderate pricing power; legacy segment weakness and absent source-addressed pass-through evidence prevent a stronger band.
catalysts: Full-year constant-currency revenue growth expectation of 4-5% and about $1B YoY FCF increase
multi-year quantum commercialization investment and enterprise AI portfolio expansion
risks: valuation still above several IT-services peer multiples
company-underwriting.thesis: IBM combines durable enterprise relationships, hybrid-cloud/AI software, consulting and infrastructure with meaningful cross-division leverage; the opportunity is credible but current consolidated growth, acquisition intensity and monetization uncertainty keep the thesis below exceptional.
company-underwriting.keyRisk: Strategic AI/quantum investment and acquisitions may fail to outgrow legacy portfolio drag or earn adequate returns on the enlarged capital base.
company-underwriting.nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 earnings on or around 2026-10-21, testing the 4-5% constant-currency revenue and higher-FCF outlook.

thesisQuality.basis: Durable enterprise modernization demand, recurring software footprint and cross-portfolio adoption are evidenced, but consolidated growth and monetization dispersion cap the score in the strong band.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q2 revenue +1%, H1 operating cash flow improved, FCF roughly flat, with strong Software/Data offset by Infrastructure and IBM Z declines plus acquisition-driven balance-sheet pressure.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Sep-25 market data showed about $225.51/share, ~20x trailing P/E, ~17.7x forward P/E and ~15.4x P/FCF: materially below IBM's recent valuation peaks but not deeply discounted versus IT-services peers.

catalystScore.basis: Identifiable Q3 earnings follow-through, raised/updated full-year operating expectations, AI portfolio execution and funded quantum roadmap provide credible catalysts, though quantum economics remain distant.

governancePower.basis: Long-duration shareholder distributions, explicit productivity discipline and investment commitments support adequate-to-strong stewardship, while acquisition intensity and unproven quantum returns prevent an 80 anchor.

alignment2036.basis: Hybrid cloud, enterprise AI, secure infrastructure and quantum R&D map strongly to long-duration digital infrastructure needs, but not all future initiatives have proven economic value.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Software, Consulting and Infrastructure reuse IBM's enterprise relationships and integration capability across multiple demand engines; evidence supports an exceptional-band entry but legacy drag prevents a higher value.

bottleneckControl.basis: Enterprise integration, mainframe installed base, Red Hat ecosystem and specialized quantum capability create meaningful switching/qualification friction, but IBM does not control an irreplaceable near-term system bottleneck.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Diversification across software, consulting, infrastructure and financing provides multiple demand paths, offset by legacy cyclicality and acquisition integration exposure.

substitutionResilience.basis: Enterprise switching costs, Red Hat/hybrid-cloud positioning and installed infrastructure support resilience, while competitive cloud/AI substitutes and legacy platform decline remain material.

supplyChainResilience.basis: IBM reports supply-chain optimization and operates a diversified portfolio, but current evidence does not establish tested multi-source redundancy sufficient for an 80 anchor.

pricingPower.basis: High consolidated gross margin and software mix support meaningful value capture, but direct contract pass-through/scarcity-rent evidence is incomplete and legacy segments remain pressured.

riskEvidence.basis: Moderate risk reflects modest consolidated growth, legacy declines, $62B debt, acquisition integration and uncertain AI/quantum monetization despite strong liquidity/cash generation.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Primary SEC/issuer evidence covers operations, cash flow, debt and strategic investment and independent current market data covers valuation; confidence is reduced by unquantified organic growth, AI-attributable economics, customer concentration and supply redundancy.

scoreRecord.thesis: IBM's enterprise installed base and hybrid-cloud/AI portfolio create durable cross-division leverage, but modest current growth and capital intensity temper the score.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Legacy drag and acquisition/quantum capital deployment fail to produce sufficient incremental organic cash returns.
